Issued at 305 PM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

This afternoon through Friday Night... 

Current surface analysis depicts a low pressure system approaching 
from the west while an associated warm front lifts north. Scattered 
showers and a few embedded thunderstorms are now beginning to push 
into central Indiana. Additional convective development can be 
expected as the disturbance pushes across the area later today into 
tonight. 

Surface observations suggest the warm front is near far southern 
portions of central Indiana where dewpoints are now in the lower 
70s. The warm front will continue lifting northward towards the I-70 
corridor. Low-level theta-e advection combined with diurnal heating 
is expected to promote MLCAPE values of 750 to as high as 1250 J/KG 
locally later this afternoon into the evening. Meanwhile aloft, a 
mid-level jet streak from the parent trough continues to shift 
eastward promoting stronger deep-layer shear. Increasing deep-layer 
shear in addition to modest destabilization could result in isolated 
severe thunderstorms. Effective shear values exceeding 40 kt are 
expected which favors the potential for supercells or organized 
storm clusters. 

Enlarging low-level veering hodographs from the warm front lifting 
north could support isolated tornadoes. Damaging wind gusts also 
appear possible with organized storm clusters. One caveat limiting 
confidence for the overall severe weather threat is uncertainty on 
the degree of low-level buoyancy. Forecast soundings from the latest 
CAMs depict poor lapse rates and relatively long-skinny CAPE 
profiles. This suggest updraft strength may be limited. However, 
even weak to modest low-level buoyancy in the favorable kinematic 
environment could support isolated damaging wind gusts or tornadoes 
so mesoscale trends will be monitored closely. Modest instability 
will greatly limit the threat for severe hail though sub-severe hail 
still appears possible.

Expect a cold front to move through late tonight advecting cooler-
drier air into the area. Look for precipitation chances to diminish 
from west to east during the late overnight. Increasingly breezy 
conditions are likely due to a tightening pressure gradient behind 
the departing front and steepening low-level lapse rates. Wind gusts 
between 25 to 35 mph should be common into Friday with sporadic 
gusts as high as 40 mph. Steepening lapse rates and marginal low-
level moisture ahead of a backdoor cold front moving through late 
Friday will promote scattered convective showers. The parent mid-
upper level trough overhead by this point should provide additional 
forcing for convection. 

Scattered lingering showers are possible early Friday night, mainly 
across northwest portions of central Indiana, before the 
aforementioned system shifts further east. Temperatures will drop 
into the upper 30s and low 40s Friday night due to the additional 
shot of cooler air. Patchy frost cannot be ruled out in sheltered 
locations into Saturday morning, but breezy conditions should mostly 
limit the threat elsewhere.

Saturday through the middle of next week...

A broad longwave trough will anchor across the eastern CONUS on 
Saturday as a strong  surface anticyclone shifts from the Upper 
Mississippi Valley southeastward across the Ohio Valley through 
Sunday. The core of the cold pool will sit overhead Saturday, 
keeping 850 mb temperatures around 0C to +2C. Despite clearing skies 
and subsidence, daytime highs on Saturday will struggle to reach out 
of the mid 50s, 10-15 degrees below normal.

Saturday night into Sunday morning represents the primary frost and 
low-end freeze window of the period. The surface high center will 
settle directly over central Indiana by 09Z Sunday, decoupling the 
boundary layer and yielding calm winds, clear skies, and a very dry 
ambient air mass with dew points in the upper 20s to low 30s. Strong 
radiational cooling will cause overnight minimum temperatures to 
drop into the lower to mid-30s across the entire forecast area, with 
rural drainage basins and traditional cold spots likely dropping 
near freezing. Widespread frost is expected across central Indiana, 
and freeze conditions are probable in sheltered rural areas. Frost 
and freeze headlines will likely be required as confidence remains 
high across deterministic GFS, ECMWF, and their respective ensemble 
suites.

The anticyclone will drift eastward toward the Mid-Atlantic on 
Sunday, allowing insolation to rebound highs into the upper 50s and 
lower 60s. Lows Sunday night will remain cool, in the upper 30s to 
lower 40s, with patchy frost confined to far eastern rural valleys 
before low-level winds back to the south.
